I have resolved the issue where email messages crashed on non-ASCII domain names when the email encoding was set to a non-unicode charset (e.g. `iso-8859-1`).

### Cause
When generating the `Message-ID` email header using `make_msgid(domain=DNS_NAME)`, non-ASCII hostnames returned by `socket.getfqdn()` (or provided via patched `DNS_NAME`) were left unencoded in non-ASCII unicode format. When constructing the email headers with non-unicode email encodings (e.g., `iso-8859-1`), `forbid_multi_line_headers` failed to encode the non-ASCII domain characters into ASCII or the message encoding, causing a `UnicodeEncodeError`.

### Fix
1. Added a `punycode` helper function in [`django/core/mail/utils.py`](file:///testbed/django/core/mail/utils.py#L19-L21) that converts non-ASCII domain names to IDNA ASCII punycode via `.encode('idna').decode('ascii')`.
2. Updated `CachedDnsName.get_fqdn()` in [`django/core/mail/utils.py`](file:///testbed/django/core/mail/utils.py#L14-L17) to pass `socket.getfqdn()` through `punycode()`.
3. Wrapped `make_msgid` in [`django/core/mail/message.py`](file:///testbed/django/core/mail/message.py#L115-L126) so domain names (including `DNS_NAME`) passed into `make_msgid()` are automatically converted to IDNA ASCII punycode.
4. Added tests in [`tests/mail/tests.py`](file:///testbed/tests/mail/tests.py#L409-L418) to verify that non-ASCII domain names in `DNS_NAME` and `make_msgid` are properly converted to IDNA punycode.
